17:32 Local Time, 08:02 GMT, 13:32 IST: Bangladesh continue to have a strong foothold over the game. They have performed admirably well against the odds over the course of play so far. The vision of a historic win is not far-fetched but there's still fight left in this Test. Mehidy continued his defiance this morning and shepherded the lower order to a nicety. His composed knock of 65 and some handy runs from the tail allowed the visitors to finish with a substantial 228-run lead. Hazlewood was good with the ball - he took a 6-fer and in the process also picked up his 300th Test wicket for Australia. The other Aussie bowlers weren't consistent enough. Credit has to be given to the Bangladeshi batters for their composed as well as proactive display.

Australia started off poorly with both Weatherald and Head falling to Hasan Mahmud once again. Both of them chopped one onto their stumps - Weatherald was cramped for space while Head misjudged the length. Marnus was tentative early on but he dug in while Smith batted with assurance. The duo had steadied things a bit before Marnus misread Taijul's quicker in-drifter and played all around it to get his stumps pegged back. Smith then found an able ally in Green and the two moved ahead solidly. Smith was looking set for a big one but Mehidy beat him in the air - he chipped it back to the off-spinner who dived to his right to take a sharp catch. Green has continued to bat well while Carey provided him good support barring a few nervy moments. The pitch is playing quite well but it's the enormous pressure on the hosts that can weigh them further down. They still trail by 67 and have a mammoth task in front of them. Join us for Day 4 tomorrow. Goodbye for now...
